findings.title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
findings.body: The delete-cache success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper does not provide a default refetch callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so a successful deletion can leave the old timestamp and Delete cached data action visible until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve persistent cache records for in-memory delegated credentials
findings.body: For delegated connections represented by negative, in-memory credential IDs, querying CalendarCache by the displayed credentialId cannot find their cache records. The cache repository explicitly supports serving these connections from persistent records using userId and the calendar key instead. Consequently, a delegated calendar can actively serve cached availability while this endpoint returns cacheUpdatedAt: null, hiding both status and deletion controls. Resolve the corresponding persistent cache records within the current user's scope and support that same mapping in the deletion handler.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE="../.env" is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory rather than the application's environment file. The script reports success, but the application never receives GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before selecting the environment file.

findings.title: Use a portable in-place replacement for the webhook URL
findings.body: The sed -i '' syntax works with BSD sed but fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the replacement fails and the script still prints that it updated the file, leaving the application pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a cross-platform replacement and check its exit status before reporting success.
